title: 8 heads (HEAD_DIM 64) at 2^18 batch / device batch 128
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (n_head 4->8 at dim 512, params/FLOPs/VRAM identical) stacked on TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128; nothing else touched.
reflection: val_bpb 0.993599, 470.0M tokens, 1793 steps, MFU 37.6%, peak VRAM 45.0GB. Two separable readings. (1) The throughput claim is CONFIRMED: device batch 128 restored MFU to 37.6% (per-step log sat at 39-40%) vs 33.4-33.9% for all five device-batch-64 replicas, and bought 470M tokens vs their 416-462M. VRAM doubled to 45GB, still inside the card. (2) Head count shows NO gain I can defend. Against the 5-replica token regression from round 0 (slope -0.000097 bpb per 1M tokens, mean 0.99609 at 426M), 470M tokens alone predicts ~0.9918; I scored 0.9936, i.e. ~0.0018 WORSE than predicted, well inside the 0.0019 replication sd but with no hint of a positive effect. Honest conclusion: 4 heads at dim 512 was not a bottleneck, and I would not spend a slot on HEAD_DIM 32. The head-dim contrast is properly read against a1/a2's (2^18,128) replicas, which are the same file minus this one line. Methodological note for the cell: my run also does not beat the standing baseline 0.992664, but that number is a cold-GPU artifact of identical code, so 'lost the round' and 'the change is bad' are not the same statement here.
